issues.description: Method signature mismatch for SealSaloon.checkOrderReady: The problem statement (UML and narrative) specifies a public no-argument method checkOrderReady(): void that should be invoked as checkOrderReady() when new orders arrive (see UML lines and narrative explaining calls). The solution implementation instead defines public void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging) (adds a boolean parameter) and calls it as checkOrderReady(true) from orderMeal. This discrepancy means students implementing or calling checkOrderReady() as specified will not match the provided solution API and may be confused about the required signature and how to invoke it.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the implementation and the specification. Prefer changing the solution to provide the public no-argument method required by the spec: add public void checkOrderReady() and (if internal logging is desired) implement a private helper overload private void checkOrderReady(boolean enableLogging). Update all internal calls (e.g., orderMeal) to invoke the public no-arg method so the public API matches the problem statement and students' expected implementation.

issues.description: Contradictory instructions about the SealSaloon.stock attribute in the problem statement: one passage instructs that the SealSaloon attributes (including stock) "should be initialized to default values (e.g., ... in the constructor of SealSaloon)" while another passage explicitly requires that the stock attribute must be static final (shared across instances). Initializing a static final field in an instance constructor is contradictory and will confuse students about whether stock is per-instance or shared and where it should be initialized. The solution resolves this by declaring and initializing the static final stock at declaration.
issues.suggestedFix: Clarify the problem statement. Either (A) keep stock as static final (shared across instances) and instruct students that it should be initialized at declaration or in a static initializer (remove the instruction to initialize it in the instance constructor), or (B) if the intent is per-instance stock, change the specification and UML to make stock a non-static final field and show initialization in the constructor. Prefer option (A) to match the solution and make the initialization location explicit.
